I have 16.1 mu and five mouths to feed. Three years in, I'm still learning, but I watch what the older farmers around me do and I follow what the agricultural station recommends when they come by.

My land splits naturally: about 6 mu I keep for wheat and maize together — wheat in winter, then I rotate to maize on the same ground after harvest. That land works hard but it's my food security and I sell the surplus. The other 10.1 mu I put into vegetables — eggplant is my main money crop, I know it best now, so I give it 5 mu. Then cabbage gets 3 mu and cauliflower gets 2.1 mu. Vegetables pay better per mu than grain.

For seeds, I buy hybrid maize every year — everyone around here uses Zhengdan 958 or similar, the yields are just better. For wheat I use an improved variety from the county seed station. For my vegetables I also buy hybrid seed packets from the market in town. It costs more but I've seen the difference.

I fertilize heavily on vegetables because that's where my income comes from. I've heard I might use too much nitrogen but I'm not sure how to cut it without risking the yield. I irrigate from my well — wheat gets watered at key stages, vegetables more often because they wilt fast in summer. I plough the grain fields in autumn and use the rotary tiller for vegetables since it's faster between crops.

Pesticide — I spray when I see problems and I do a couple of preventive sprays on eggplant because last year I lost some plants to disease and it hurt.
